Pulastya
------------------------------------------
One of the problems we come across in Hindu mythological literature is the names of the ṛṣis or the sages. Whereas there can be several sages of the same name, living at different periods of time, the same sage can also have several names. One such enigma is that of the sage पुलस्त्य.
The information gathered about him from various sources like the epics and the पुराणस् may be summarised as follows:
He was one of the mānasaputras—mind-born sons—of the creator ब्रह्मा. He was also one of the great sages in the group of सप्तर्षिस् (the Seven Sages).
He had several wives: Go, Havirbhuk, Ilabilā, Prīti, सन्ध्या and Pratīcyā.
It is likely that some of these names may refer to the same woman.
Viśravas, the ड़थेर् of रावण and his brothers, as also कुबेर, was पुलस्त्य’s son.
Once रावण was imprisoned by कार्तवीर्यार्जुन, a mighty king. पुलस्त्य had to intercede on his behalf and get him released.
It was पुलस्त्य who inspired the sage पराशर to compose the famous Viṣṇupurāṇa.
Once पराशर started a sacrifice to destroy all the राक्षसस् since one of them (Kalmāṣapāda) had killed his ड़थेर् शक्ति, the son of वसिष्ठ. But पुलस्त्य successfully persuaded him to give it up.
Bhīṣma, the grandsire of the Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas, learnt about the greatness of many places of पिल्ग्रिमगे, from the sage पुलस्त्य.
